articles.title: Midea PortaSplit : le climatiseur mobile star de l’été revient en stock à -100 € (mais pas pour longtemps)
articles.text:
Le Midea PortaSplit est le climatiseur qui s’arrache depuis le début de l’été. La demande a été telle qu’il s’est retrouvé en rupture un peu partout, et que certains vendeurs l’ont facturé jusqu’à 1 500 euros. À 899 euros, on revient à un tarif raisonnable, à condition d’attraper le stock au vol.
Pour rappel, le PortaSplit fonctionne comme un climatiseur split classique, mais sans travaux. Une unité intérieure mobile est reliée à une petite unité extérieure posée sur le rebord de fenêtre ou le balcon, sans perçage ni installateur.
Jusqu’au 31 Août, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500 perd 300 € ! Sans fil périmétrique, 360° LiDAR & double caméra IA, pente 80%, DropMow, auto cartographie… Bref, elle a tout ce qu’il faut pour vous permettre de ne plus jamais tondre votre pelouse !
Côté fiche technique : 12 000 BTU (soit 3,5 kW de froid), classe énergétique A++ en froid, 39 décibels en mode silencieux et un pilotage par Wi-Fi. Il assure aussi un chauffage réversible pour la mi-saison et vise des pièces jusqu’à 40 m². Midea a d’ailleurs réorganisé ses usines pour expédier 200 000 unités en Europe cet été.
899 euros, un bon plan ou pas ?
À 899 euros chez Joybuy (une entreprise chinoise avec des entrepôts en France), on paie 100 euros de moins que le prix officiel, et surtout bien moins que les tarifs gonflés vus chez certains vendeurs. Ce n’est pas le prix plancher pour autant. En passant par l’Allemagne, quelques acheteurs ont réussi à économiser jusqu’à 250 euros. Le PortaSplit tourne aussi au gaz R32, que l’Europe compte interdire à la vente neuve à partir de 2029. Rien de bloquant pour un achat aujourd’hui, mais autant le savoir.
Le vrai obstacle reste la disponibilité. Le produit repasse en stock par fenêtres de quelques dizaines de minutes, toutes les 6 à 8 heures environ, avant de retomber en rupture.
Les délais de livraison s’allongent au fil des commandes : un achat passé le 11 août était annoncé pour le 18, un autre du 13 août pour le 25. Pour comprendre quand espérer un réassort, mieux vaut activer les alertes et rester patient.
À 899 euros, l’affaire tient la route pour qui vise précisément ce modèle et accepte de surveiller les réapprovisionnements. Si vous pouvez patienter ou regarder du côté allemand durant l’hiver, vous paierez sans doute un peu moins. Pour comparer avec d’autres options, notre comparatif des climatiseurs mobiles fait le tri.
Le Midea PortaSplit est proposé à 899 euros sur Joybuy, quand le stock le permet.

articles.title: Critical VMware vCenter Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
articles.text:
Threat actors have started exploiting a recently patched critical-severity vulnerability in VMware vCenter, rapid incident response company Quirso reports.
The bug was disclosed on July 29, when Broadcom patched it alongside four other security defects in multiple VMware products.
Tracked as CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS score of 9.8), the flaw is described as a directory traversal issue in the Syslog server that leads to remote code execution.
“A malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to execute arbitrary code,” Broadcom’s advisory reads.
According to Quirso, an advanced persistent threat (APT) actor has been exploiting web-accessible VMware vCenter servers vulnerable to CVE-2026-59310, using a reverse shell for persistent access.
The cybersecurity company identified over 360 victim IP addresses across 47 countries, half of which are distributed across only five countries: Germany, the US, Turkey, Iran, and France.
“The exact number of victim organizations cannot be inferred from these IP addresses, as an IP address does not necessarily correspond to a unique company or physical system. Some addresses belong to hosting providers, cloud networks, or shared infrastructure,” Quirso says.
According to the company, the exploitation started on August 3, with over 340 victim IP addresses seen connecting to the attackers’ infrastructure by August 5.
“While the attacker might have had prior knowledge of the vulnerability, the strong correlation between the time of disclosure and exploitation suggests the disclosure as the initial starting point for the campaign,” Quirso notes.
Following initial compromise, the attackers dropped the open source SSH reverse shell framework reverse_ssh to maintain an outbound control connection from the compromised systems, bypassing security controls that typically block inbound connections.
Quirso released a generic YARA rule for identifying reverse_ssh builds. As the tool can also be used for legitimate penetration testing, organizations with publicly accessible vCenter systems are advised to validate any detections by also looking for unauthorized installations and unexpected outbound connections and execution.

articles.title: Microchip Switchtec 160-Lane PCIe Gen6 Switch Shown at FMS 2026 with XpressConnect PCIe 6 Retimer
articles.text:
At FMS 2026, Microchip had a number of its data center connectivity solutions on display. That included a new family of Microchip Switchtec PCIe Gen6 switches with up to 160 lanes. We also saw the company’s XpressConnect PCIe Gen6 retimer chip working. There was even a cameo by an Everpure DirectFlash module that we caught at the Microchip booth. Let us get to it.
Microchip Switchtec PFX 160xG6 Switch Shown at FMS 2026
First, we saw a Microchip Switchtec PFX 160xG6 switch mounted on a test PCB.
This is a new generation of PCIe switch chip designed to compete with offerings from Broadcom, Astera Labs, and Marvell. Realistically, Broadcom has been the big player in the PCIe switch space since the Avago-PLX acquisition over a decade ago. Microchip has kept its Switchtec line going, and we have covered the line in the past. The space has been heating up as PCIe switches went from tools mostly in storage servers and the fringe deep learning servers of yesteryear to critical components in modern AI infrastructure build-outs.
Microchip was showing the PFX 160xG6, which is a 160-lane PCIe Gen6 switch chip. The company also has a PSX line, which, from what I understand, is more of a programmable line used for a storage platform.
These switches can have up to 20 ports but usually use far fewer because they are often connected to x16 GPUs and NICs these days. Notably, while other vendors are focusing on PCIe and CXL switches in the Gen6 generation, Microchip seems to be focusing more on PCIe.
Microchip XpressConnect PCIe Gen6 Retimer Shown
On the PCIe Gen6 and CXL side, we also saw the Microchip XpressConnect PCIe Gen6 retimer in action.
Retimers are important in today’s architectures even as NVIDIA has been trying to design around their use. The reason is that PCIe Gen6 signaling generally has shorter reach, and yet systems are growing in size due to the sheer number of components and the cooling they require. As a result, this is a hot area in the industry. A PCIe retimer, if you recall, is a device that helps retime a signal, thereby extending the effective reach of the link.
Here you can see the board running live on the show floor retiming a link. Part of me things the engineers just have fun stacking CEM cards and various cables to make these demos.
Microchip’s XpressConnect can also retime CXL 3.1. That is important since this market has taken off and competition like the Astera Labs Aries 6 can do CXL as well.
It is an interesting and competitive space with companies Broadcom, Marvell, and Phison all working on solutions.
Bonus: Everpure DirectFlash Module on Display
As Sam and I were walking through the booth, we also saw an Everpure DirectFlash module. Usually we see models like this, so we do not get to see who is running inside the module, but being in the Microchip booth, we have some idea.
This may not seem like a big one, but this week, Everpure announced that a second top 5 hyper-scaler will be using its DirectFlash technology in a big win for the company. The first hyper-scaler using it is Meta, from what we understand.
It is always fun to see what you can learn when you walk the FMS show floor, finding things like this.
Final Words
I am at Microchip MASTERs today in Phoenix, AZ, in a nice break from the 26 flights in 46 days schedule. Hopefully, I will learn something neat and get a Substack post up on the event. In the meantime, we wanted to show some of the fun things that we saw at FMS last week and cover some of Microchip’s PCIe Gen6 solutions.

articles.title: I looked inside an AI generated movie, and the best parts were all human
articles.text:
Imagine a trio of bumbling, English lads who fantasize about becoming megastars while knocking back a few pints in a grimy pub somewhere in London. Picture the guys chortling and trying to one-up each other’s idealized visions of the future with a series of increasingly glitzy fantasies in which their fame leads to access to groupies and lavish parties on luxurious boats. Imagine these men are actually characters in a film — one filled with hyperkinetic smash cuts to action sequences in which they’re fighting or running from armed goons. This movie might be the sort of feature you’d expect from directors like Edgar Wright or Guy Ritchie. But all of this actually comes from Cully Hill Boys, the latest project from the AI filmmaking platform Higgsfield.
I looked inside an AI generated movie, and the best parts were all human
Higgsfield is using Cully Hill Boys to show you how to prompt up your own movie.
Cully Hill Boys is one of the few AI movies out this year that comes anywhere near close to looking and feeling like a traditionally produced feature. A large part of the movie’s strength is almost certainly rooted in how much Wright and Ritchie’s style has been baked into it, and it’s not just visual inspiration. In addition to posting Cully Hill Boys online, Higgsfield published many of the prompts that were used to make it. Several of those prompts mention Wright and Ritchie by name, which, along with a script written by a real screenwriter, underlines how the best parts of these films are undeniably taken from actual human artists.
Cully Hill Boys tells the story of three struggling rappers from East London whose lives are turned upside down when they accidentally steal a crime lord’s money. The project is codirected by Adilet Abish and Aitore Zholdaskali — who also helmed Higgsfield’s Hell Grind feature — and is based on a script that was initially written by Tim Planagan before it landed on the Black List screenplay submission service for unproduced projects. After acquiring the script’s AI production rights, Higgsfield tapped streamer Mikyle “N3on” Rafiq, basketball content creator Matt Kiatipis, and UFC fighter Israel Adesanya to “star” as its leads. Though none of Cully Hill Boys’ actors shot any scenes on set, each of them signed licensing agreements with Higgsfield for their likenesses to be used in the project. And while Planagan gave Higgsfield the ability to adapt this story using generative AI, he still retains the rights necessary for it to be produced traditionally.
Rather than trying to release Cully Hill Boys in theaters, Higgsfield — another service that sells access to various AI models — uploaded the film and most of its constituent prompts online in order to showcase what’s possible with its Cinema Studio suite of AI filmmaking tools. The film also functions as a gigantic ad for Higgsfield’s newly added Seedance 2.5 functionality, and to highlight new ways that studios can collaborate with digital creators.
What’s most striking about Cully Hill Boys as you begin to watch it is the way its story moves much in the same way most direct-to-video action / comedies usually do. We’re introduced to Cal (Kiatipis), Horace (Rafiq), and Oli (Adesanya) as a trio of longtime friends who just can’t figure out how to realize their dreams of becoming well-known musicians. After establishing the boys’ interpersonal dynamics, the film zooms out to show us more about who they are individually. Oli’s mom insists that he gets a real job, Cal’s ex doesn’t believe he can be a good father to their daughter, and Horace doesn’t have a lot going on outside of being the group’s designated driver. Cully Hill Boys establishes all of these details in its first few minutes with a series of scenes that flow together with a tonal and visual smoothness that you seldom see from AI films regardless of their length.
Cully Hill Boys’ story was crafted by a human with an understanding of proper pacing.
Some of that likely boils down to the way that Seedance 2.5 is capable of churning out much longer (about 30 seconds) clips than other video generation models. With films created with AI video models that only generate a few seconds of footage at a time, you can usually see and hear exactly when clips have been stitched together as a way to work around the technology’s limitations. There’s still some of that in Cully Hill Boys, but many of the project’s scenes unfold at a pace that feels much more organic and closer to what you might expect from a traditionally made feature.
Watching the movie, I got the sense its plot’s general cohesion was a reflection of Zholdaskali and Abish — who led a team of nine other directors, according to Higgsfield — closely following the beats of Planagan’s script. Planagan has said that he doesn’t use AI tools in his writing process, and it definitely feels like Cully Hill Boys is a stronger film than Hell Grind because its core narrative was crafted by an experienced, human storyteller with an understanding of proper pacing. There’s a clear logic to characters’ dialog, and the avatars have a passable emotiveness that speaks to how Higgsfield created them using photos and audio clips provided by real people. But when you pay close attention to things like incomprehensible text in books and the way that characters often have a distracting lack of chemistry, it’s easy to clock that most of the movie was made by feeding prompts into various generative models.
Scrolling through Higgsfield’s official Cully Hill Boys page, it’s actually fascinating to see how many different iterations of individual shots the film’s creative team generated using text prompts. Anthropic’s Claude was used to come up with prompts, which were sent to Seedance 2.5 to create video and speech, while ByteDance’s Seedream and Google’s Nano Banana were used for image and video editing. Per the website, Cully Hill Boys’ creative leads had to split their workflow across different models “because the rules of one job poison the other.” That meant, for example, one instance of Claude had to be focused solely on churning out prompts with wording specifically designed to generate workable images while another was dedicated to doing the same for prompts that would eventually become videos clips.
Similar to how Cully Hill Boys as a whole feels like an ad for Higgsfield as one of the many AI filmmaking platforms out there, the company’s transparency about how the film was made comes across as a way to highlight all of the models it gives its users access to. Reading the text prompts — most of which were in English, while some were in Simplified Chinese — you can see how detailed their descriptions are. But when you compare specific prompts to their corresponding scenes in the full movie, it becomes clear that these models aren’t just whipping up impressive shots and camera movements out of thin air. It’s evident there’s an extra bit of human work guiding this project.
More than a few of the prompts related to Cully Hill Boys’ zippier, more action-packed scenes reference elements of Wright and Ritchie’s styles of filmmaking. The prompts didn’t contain explicit directions to mimic any specific one of Wright or Ritchie films, but they did include asks for “GUY RITCHIE COVERAGE” and “DYNAMIC clip-style (Edgar Wright snap.)” It’s not unusual for traditional directors to pay homage by replicating one another’s signature filmmaking techniques. But Cully Hill Boys’ is a different sort of beast because its production process seemingly hinges on its underlying AI models having first been trained on Wright and Ritchie’s IP in order to understand when they’re being asked to generate similar footage.
As impressive as Cully Hill Boys is compared to other AI movies, it feels more like a (mostly) polished proof of concept than a project that’s ready for the mainstream spotlight. Rafiq, Kiatipis, and Adesanya’s fans might get a kick out of seeing their faves in a feature-length production, but this probably isn’t something that most moviegoers would be keen to watch. Higgsfield likely understands that reality. Cully Hill Boys’ real value is in its potential to further normalize the idea of AI movies in people’s minds.

articles.title: E-bike com visual de moto combina diversão, praticidade e condução acessível
articles.text:
A Super73 apresentou a MZFT, uma bicicleta elétrica de inspiração motociclística que combina visual robusto, acelerador no guidão e dimensões compactas. O modelo pertence à Classe 2, tem motor de 500 W e velocidade máxima de 20 mph.
Testada pela jornalista Heather Kuldell-Ware, da Popular Science, a bicicleta foi utilizada em deslocamentos urbanos, pequenos trajetos e um percurso de 25 km com diferentes tipos de terreno. A avaliação apontou autonomia compatível com a proposta de uso recreativo e cotidiano.
O modelo custa a partir de US$ 1.995 na configuração com uma bateria de 520 Wh. Entre os principais diferenciais estão a altura de assento de 27 polegadas, o compartimento de armazenamento sob o banco e a possibilidade de instalação de uma segunda bateria.
Uma e-bike feita para parecer diferente
A MZFT foi concebida para se afastar da aparência tradicional das bicicletas elétricas. O desenho combina referências de bicicletas BMX dos anos 1980 e motos de trilha, enquanto os pneus largos de 16 por 4,5 polegadas reforçam a identidade visual.
Apesar da aparência, a configuração mecânica segue a proposta de uma bicicleta elétrica Classe 2. O conjunto utiliza um motor traseiro de 500 W, transmissão de velocidade única e acelerador acionado pelo polegar. A assistência elétrica e a carga da bateria são acompanhadas por dois conjuntos de cinco LEDs.
A versão avaliada tinha bateria de 520 Wh, equivalente a 52 V e 10 Ah, com certificação UL2271. A Super73 também oferece uma configuração com duas baterias, alternativa que pode ampliar consideravelmente a distância percorrida antes de uma recarga.
A autonomia declarada pela fabricante chega a 32 km com uma bateria e 64 km na configuração dupla. No teste realizado, a MZFT percorreu um circuito de 25 km que reunia ciclovias compartilhadas, cruzamentos urbanos, uma passarela de madeira, uma subida acentuada e cerca de 1.300 pés de variação de altitude.
O motor conseguiu concluir o percurso, embora tenha sido necessário auxiliar com os pedais em algumas das subidas mais íngremes. Ao final do trajeto, ainda restavam duas das cinco luzes indicadoras da bateria. A avaliação considerou realista a autonomia de 24 a 32 km para a configuração com uma bateria.
Foco no conforto e na acessibilidade
Um dos pontos destacados na avaliação foi a altura do assento. Com 27 polegadas, a MZFT foi projetada para acomodar pessoas com estatura entre 1,47 m e 1,78 m, faixa que amplia o acesso ao segmento de bicicletas elétricas com aparência de moto.
O peso do veículo, por outro lado, chega a aproximadamente 38,6 kg. O banco largo favorece o uso descontraído com o acelerador, mas prejudica a experiência de quem pretende pedalar por períodos prolongados. A posição exigida pelas dimensões do assento deixa as pernas mais afastadas durante a pedalada.
A construção também não utiliza suspensão. Por isso, buracos, emendas do asfalto e trechos de cascalho são sentidos com maior intensidade. A avaliação indicou que a MZFT se adapta melhor a pavimentos regulares e ciclovias lisas.
Acelerador é protagonista
A experiência de condução privilegia o acelerador. Ao pressionar o comando instalado no lado direito do guidão, a bicicleta ganha velocidade sem exigir o uso constante dos pedais.
A resposta pode parecer brusca quando a bicicleta passa por irregularidades, já que movimentos involuntários do polegar podem interferir no acionamento. Ainda assim, a avaliação considerou o comportamento compatível com a proposta recreativa do modelo.
A simplicidade também aparece na ausência de recursos destinados a elevar a velocidade máxima. A MZFT permanece limitada a 20 mph e não oferece um modo oculto de Classe 3 ou configurações adicionais para ultrapassar esse limite.
Sob o banco há ainda um compartimento com trava para pequenos objetos. O espaço inclui duas portas USB-C, permitindo utilizar a estrutura para guardar itens essenciais e carregar dispositivos compatíveis.
Aparência influencia a recepção
O visual inspirado em motos também interfere na maneira como a bicicleta é percebida por outras pessoas. Durante os testes, crianças demonstraram interesse pelo desenho compacto e pelos pneus largos, enquanto alguns ciclistas tradicionais reagiram com desconfiança ao estilo do veículo.
A avaliação relacionou essa reação à crescente presença de modelos elétricos mais potentes que visualmente se aproximam de motocicletas e bicicletas de trilha. Nesse cenário, a aparência da MZFT pode provocar uma percepção diferente daquela associada às e-bikes convencionais, apesar de sua classificação como Classe 2.
A característica central do modelo está justamente nessa combinação. A MZFT procura oferecer o apelo visual e a condução por acelerador associados às bicicletas elétricas de inspiração motociclística, mas mantém pedais funcionais, limite de 20 mph e configuração correspondente à Classe 2.
Wagner Edwards é Bacharel em Jornalismo e atua como Analista de SEO e de Conteúdo no Olhar Digital. Possui experiência, também, na redação, edição e produção de textos para notícias e reportagens.

articles.title: « Seuls mais motivés » : les confidences du patron de Lapierre après la faillite d’Accell
articles.text:
Le numéro 1 européen du vélo électrique et mécanique est-il déjà en passe d’être démantelé ? L’échec de reprise par le Singapourien Dutech a entraîné un sursis de paiement le 5 août, puis la banqueroute des six filiales néerlandaises le 11 août.
Nous avons ainsi voulu comprendre quel avenir se dessine pour les différentes entités et marques, dont celle de Lapierre. Nous avons pu nous entretenir avec le Directeur Général de la firme française, William Perrier, pour détailler sa situation et son activité en France.
Un rappel utile sur le poids de l’entreprise : fondée en 1946 à Dijon, Lapierre revendique 106 salariés, plus de 800 revendeurs et 99,1 millions d’euros de chiffre d’affaires en 2025.
Lapierre concentrée sur un plan de sauvetage, une quinzaine d’investisseurs déjà en contact
“On a fait la demande au tribunal de commerce mercredi dernier, le calendrier judiciaire fait que l’on ne peut pas le rencontrer avant le 25 août”, déclare William Perrier, « donc nous ne sommes pas encore sous leur protection judiciaire”.
“Pendant cette période-là, on essaie de comprendre tous les montages menés lors des précédentes restructurations financières, leurs impacts et implications pour Lapierre” précise le DG de la marque française, “on a deux objectifs, la lecture la plus complète possible pour le tribunal de commerce, et affiner le plan que l’on souhaite présenter”.
“On souhaite que Lapierre redevienne Lapierre et s’inscrive durablement sur le marché français dans un premier temps” décrit le dirigeant, “on verra ensuite l’ouverture sur d’autres marchés dans un second temps”.
Ainsi le rôle de William Perrier a basculé de l’opérationnel vers l’élaboration de ce plan, afin de solliciter et séduire de nouveaux investisseurs. Mais tout cela semble ainsi s’organiser loin du reste du groupe Accell, non ?
Lapierre « seule » face à Accell, un patron déterminé à sauver la marque, avec déjà des investisseurs
“Nous n’avons quasiment plus d’interactions avec le groupe ou les autres entités à l’heure actuelle, sinon avec les administrateurs des entités néerlandaise ou des autres liquidées” confie-t-il, “je considère que nous sommes seuls avec Lapierre, ainsi qu’avec la marque espagnole Comet, qui est aussi très bien implantée localement”.
“On ne peut évidemment faire aucune promesse, car la situation est instable et mouvante” déclare le DG de Cycles Lapierre, “mais je peux dire que nous sommes proactifs et motivés pour assurer un avenir viable pour l’entreprise”. Il nous confie aussi avoir été contacté par « une quinzaine d’investisseurs », sans préciser leur nom ou leur intérêt.
Il ajoute toutefois qu’une reprise partielle du groupe avec les marques de la filiale allemande Winora-Staiger (Winora, Haibike, Ghost) reste possible en théorie, mais qu’il est actuellement « trop chronophage de discuter avec leurs représentants ».
Rappel, elle se trouve actuellement en insolvabilité et en auto-administration. Concernant l’offre de rachat intégral du groupe par Quanta Capital, le directeur de Lapierre n’a reçu « aucune sollicitation » à l’heure actuelle.
Pour rappel, Quanta Capital est une société d’investissement basée à Dublin, dirigée par l’ancien coureur cycliste Mel Sutcliffe. Elle a confirmé étudier une offre sur l’intégralité du groupe Accell, en s’appuyant sur plusieurs investisseurs et une institution financière, sans donner de calendrier ferme.
Les livraisons et le SAV Lapierre continuent en France, mais l’investissement est nécessaire pour les VAE
“Les ventes ne sont pas arrêtées, on continue de vendre des vélos et des pièces détachées, tout comme les livraisons et de gérer le SAV” confirme William Perrier. Mais la suspension de la production du site hongrois d’Accell a-t-elle des répercussions ?
“Effectivement, la production s’est arrêtée pour les vélos électriques, tout comme celle à Dijon mais pour les vacances, ce qui était déjà programmé”, explique-t-il, “on peut continuer avec les pièces actuelles car nous avons du stock et des alternatives pour les prochaines semaines”.
Il ajoute toutefois devoir “trouver rapidement de l’investissement pour que les VAE soient assemblés de manières différente” à moyen et long terme. Sur ces derniers, l’équipe travaille sur “un plan global pour permettre à Lapierre d’exister et au consommateur de retrouver toutes les gammes le plus rapidement possible”.
Les marques allemandes encore en attente, Babboe dans le flou
Quid des autres marques vendues en France ? « Pour les marques allemandes [Winora, Haibike et Ghost], il faut encore déterminer le niveau de service que l’on pourra donner, précise le DG, car nous n’avons encore eu que sept jours pour travailler. L’objectif premier reste Lapierre. » Il ne peut ainsi donner d’indication pour les autres marques néerlandaises (Babboe, Carqon, etc).
Nous avons tenté de contacter plusieurs personnes au sein de Babboe, pour l’instant sans réponse. Nous communiquerons sur ce point dès que nous aurons d’amples informations. Pour rappel, l’entreprise néerlandaise vient à peine de se relever de son rappel et remplacement de 22 000 cadres, mais une fondation se manifeste déjà pour ne pas délaisser ses clients.
Pour terminer sur Lapierre, il faudra ainsi patienter au minimum jusqu’au 25 août pour l’ouverture de l’étape judiciaire, avec de potentielles informations sur l’avenir de la marque française.

articles.title: From Tokens To Tasks: Why Agentic AI Changes The Infrastructure Conversation
articles.text:
As AI moves from answering prompts to completing work, infrastructure has to optimize the full workflow around the model.
At 8:42 a.m., a developer opens her laptop to a red build, a failing test and a release branch waiting. Instead of combing through logs, commits and repo history herself, she gives an AI coding agent a simple instruction:
“Fix the failing test. Find the bug, patch the code, run the tests and summarize what changed.”
A few keystrokes and a sip of tea later, the agent returns a tested patch and concise explanation. To the human, it feels like fast magic: intent in, outcome out. But inside the system, nothing about that outcome is simple.
That one prompt can trigger request parsing, task creation, policy checks, repo search, context assembly, tokenization, model calls, tool validation, sandbox routing, file edits, test runs, telemetry and final verification. The model call is critical, but it is only one part of the workload. The real achievement is coordinating the task graph.
Agentic AI plans, retrieves, acts, checks, retries and reports. As AI moves from isolated prompt-response interactions to continuous workflows, the unit of performance shifts from the token to the completed task.
For years, AI infrastructure has been measured largely by model execution: prefill, decode, tokens per second, latency to first token, throughput, batching efficiency, memory use and accelerator utilization. Those metrics still matter, but agentic AI widens the critical path.
A traditional inference request is bounded: prompt in, response out. An agentic workflow may plan, retrieve context, manage state, call tools and APIs, run in sandboxes, verify results, capture telemetry and retry. The output may be an answer, a code diff, a database query, a tool call or a decision to gather more evidence.
In short, agentic AI turns inference into a distributed systems problem. GPUs remain essential for heavy model execution, but the surrounding work increasingly defines system performance: what runs, where it runs, what context travels with it, which tools are allowed and whether the result satisfies intent.
That surrounding stack adds layers around the model, and much of the coordination runs through the CPU: orchestration, memory and retrieval, tool calls, runtimes and sandboxes, policy systems and observability. The model provides intelligence, reasoning and generation, and the surrounding system turns that intelligence into action.
For a chatbot, token throughput can tell us how quickly the model responds, how fast it generates and how many users the system can serve. For agentic AI, that view is incomplete.
Our developer does not experience the system as raw tokens per second. She experiences whether the bug was found, the patch was correct, the tests passed, permissions were respected and the result can be reviewed and trusted. The same is true for enterprise, research, security, operations and physical-world agents. The user cares about the outcome.
That means agentic AI needs workflow-level metrics: cost per completed task, tool-call latency, retrieval latency, sandbox startup time and agents per node. The key question shifts from “How fast did the model generate?” to “How efficiently did the system complete the task?”
The CPU’s role in agentic AI is easiest to see around the model call. Before the model runs, the system parses the request, establishes the workspace, loads policies, inspects files, queries retrieval systems, ranks context, counts tokens and prepares the request. Around the model call, the CPU handles routing, tokenization, batching, streaming and schema setup. Afterward, it validates output, routes tool calls, manages sandboxes and subprocesses, captures logs, classifies failures, updates state and assembles telemetry.
In the coding-agent example, some of the heaviest CPU work may come after the model proposes a fix: running tests, invoking compilers, starting subprocesses, classifying failures and deciding whether to retry. That work stresses cores, cache, memory, storage and orchestration software.
This is the hidden, crucial compute behind the “fast magic” of agentic AI.
As agentic systems scale, the head-node role becomes strategically important. The AI head node is not simply a CPU next to an accelerator. It is the control point that helps a heterogeneous AI system behave like one reliable service: routing requests, managing state, preparing context, coordinating accelerators, handling APIs and tools, enforcing policy, capturing telemetry and keeping the workflow observable.
Orchestration is the function: deciding what work happens, where it runs, what context travels with it, which tools are allowed and whether the task is complete. The head node is the infrastructure role that anchors that function across CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, memory, storage, networking, runtimes, databases, policy systems and observability tools.
As AI infrastructure becomes more heterogeneous, models, tools, memory, accelerators, APIs, sandboxes, policies, traces and evaluation loops all have to stay in sync. The head node is where that coordination becomes operational.
For Arm, agentic AI is a platform moment. Its infrastructure demands map directly to what cloud builders already care about: performance, efficiency, scale, software readiness and choice. The question is no longer only which system can generate tokens fastest. It is which platform can complete more workflows within real-world constraints: latency, power, cost, utilization, reliability and developer velocity.
Arm brings a compute platform built for heterogeneous infrastructure. In the agentic era, AI systems are assembled from CPUs, GPUs, accelerators, memory, storage, networking, runtimes, APIs, tools, observability systems and policy controls. Arm’s value is in helping make that broader system more efficient, scalable and easier to optimize.
That value starts with Arm’s broad technology foundation: flexible Arm Neoverse IP and Compute Subsystems (CSS) based compute platforms, software enablement and a partner ecosystem that gives AI infrastructure builders multiple ways to design and deploy infrastructure for their specific workloads. Agentic AI makes that optionality more important, because no single compute profile can efficiently serve every part of the workflow.
That is why the Arm story should be measured at the workflow level. Better agentic infrastructure should show up in outcomes such as cost per completed task, lower latency, higher utilization and more predictable execution. Those proof points connect the CPU and head-node role directly to business value.
Arm AGI CPU extends that story into Arm-designed silicon for agentic AI infrastructure, giving AI infrastructure builders another way to deploy Arm-based compute where the CPU helps coordinate the work around the model: control, memory, retrieval, tools, APIs, runtimes, sandboxes and observability.
The goal is not to diminish GPUs or accelerators. The goal is to make the full heterogeneous system work better. Agentic AI will reward infrastructure that can optimize the whole task graph, not just the token stream.
Let’s return to our tea-sipping developer. She did not ask for tokens. She asked for a fix. That is the infrastructure shift agentic AI brings. In the prompt-response era, model performance was the visible center of gravity. In the agentic era, the system must optimize the whole loop: intelligence, memory, tools, state, policy, execution, verification and observability.
The next generation of AI infrastructure will be judged by whether it can complete tasks quickly, correctly, securely, observably and efficiently. In that world, Arm AGI CPU gives AI infrastructure builders another way to deploy Arm-based compute for the orchestration and task work that helps turn model output into useful action.

articles.title: Apple offre jusqu'à 120 € aux étudiants, mais ça ne compense pas la hausse du prix des Mac
articles.text:
Apple relance son Back to School en France, un mois après les États-Unis. Le constructeur propose jusqu’à 120 € de carte cadeau pour l’achat d’un Mac ou d’un iPad au tarif étudiant.
Dans le détail, et d’après les conditions publiées par Apple, la carte cadeau atteint 80 € pour l’achat d’un iPad Air, un iPad Pro ou un MacBook Air, et monte à 120 € pour un MacBook Pro. L’offre vise les étudiants, leurs parents et les personnels des établissements scolaires. Elle tient jusqu’au 22 octobre 2026 et se cumule avec la remise habituelle de l’Apple Store Éducation. Pour en profiter, il faut passer par cette boutique et s’identifier via UNiDAYS, une vérification d’identité qu’Apple a rendue obligatoire ces derniers mois pour couper court aux abus.
L’an dernier, Apple offrait plutôt un accessoire au choix, comme des AirPods 4 d’une valeur de 199 €. La carte cadeau est plus souple, puisqu’elle sert sur l’App Store, pour un abonnement iCloud+ ou n’importe quel produit Apple. Mais sa valeur maximale a nettement baissé. L’iMac et le MacBook Neo, l’ordinateur le moins cher de la marque, sont exclus de la sélection cette année.
La carte cadeau ne rattrape pas la hausse de juin
Le 25 juin 2026, Apple a relevé les prix de la quasi-totalité de ses Mac et iPad. Le MacBook Air a pris 200 €, le MacBook Pro jusqu’à 400 €, et le MacBook Neo 100 €, passant à 799 €. La raison tient à la flambée du prix de la mémoire vive, aspirée par les centres de données qui font tourner l’intelligence artificielle. Tim Cook, le CEO d’Apple, avait prévenu quelques jours plus tôt que ces hausses étaient devenues inévitables.
Autrement dit, une carte de 80 ou 120 € ne compense pas une hausse qui a parfois dépassé 300 €. Le MacBook Air 13,6 pouces démarre à 1 289 € au tarif étudiant, contre 1 399 € en prix public. Le même modèle se trouvait fin juillet à 1 199 € chez Amazon. Les 80 € de carte cadeau aident à se rapprocher de ce tarif, sans l’égaler.
L’offre vaut surtout pour qui comptait déjà acheter un Mac ou un iPad au tarif éducation et dépenser la carte dans l’écosystème Apple pour des AirPods . Pour les autres, un tour du côté des distributeurs ou du reconditionné reste parfois plus rentable, surtout depuis la hausse de juin.

articles.title: ChatGPT gibt es jetzt auch für Linux – darauf müsst ihr aber noch verzichten
articles.text:
ChatGPT gibt es jetzt auch für Linux – doch eine wichtige Funktion fehlt
Während ChatGPT für macOS und Windows bereits als eigene Desktop-App verfügbar ist, mussten Linux-User bislang auf die Web-Version oder inoffizielle Anwendungen ausweichen. Jetzt veröffentlicht OpenAI erstmals eine offizielle ChatGPT-Desktop-App für Linux. Die Anwendung startet zunächst als Preview.
Neben ChatGPT sind auch Codex und ChatGPT Work in die Linux-App integriert. Damit können User unter anderem Coding-Aufgaben bearbeiten und umfangreichere Workflows ausführen. Besonders für Entwickler:innen könnte die neue Anwendung relevant sein, da Linux in vielen Entwicklungsumgebungen eingesetzt wird. Zum Start ist die Preview allerdings nur für bestimmte Linux-Versionen verfügbar.
Ubuntu, Debian und Fedora werden zum Start unterstützt
OpenAI bietet die Preview zunächst für ausgewählte Linux-Versionen an. Unterstützt werden drei Distributionen, also unterschiedliche Varianten des Linux-Betriebssystems:
- Ubuntu 24.04 LTS und 26.04 LTS
- Debian 13
- Fedora 43 und 44
Die Installation erfolgt über .deb- oder .rpm-Pakete. OpenAI stellt diese sowohl für Systeme mit x64- als auch ARM64-Architektur bereit.
Andere Distributionen und ältere Versionen werden zum Start nicht offiziell unterstützt. Wann OpenAI die Preview auf weitere Linux-Systeme ausweitet, hat das Unternehmen bislang nicht bekanntgegeben.
Linux-App bietet Entwicklern neue Möglichkeiten
Für Entwickler:innen wird die Linux-App vor allem durch Codex relevant. OpenAIs Coding-Agent kann unter anderem Features entwickeln, Refactorings und Migrationen durchführen sowie Tests und Code Reviews erstellen. Für umfangreichere Arbeitsprozesse steht zusätzlich ChatGPT Work zur Verfügung.
Codex ist dabei nicht auf die Desktop-App beschränkt. Der Agent kann über dasselbe ChatGPT-Konto auch im Editor und im Terminal genutzt werden. In ChatGPT lassen sich zudem mehrere Agents parallel einsetzen, um verschiedene Projekte oder Coding-Aufgaben gleichzeitig zu bearbeiten.
Die Linux-App erweitert damit auch die Möglichkeiten, ChatGPT direkt in bestehende Entwicklungsprozesse einzubinden. ChatGPT, Codex und Work können innerhalb einer gemeinsamen Desktop-Anwendung genutzt werden, während Codex zusätzlich mit Editor und Terminal verbunden werden kann. OpenAI führt damit Funktionen zusammen, die von allgemeinen KI-Aufgaben über umfangreichere Workflows bis zur Software-Entwicklung reichen.
Eine wichtige Desktop-Funktion fehlt noch
Die Preview bietet allerdings noch nicht den gleichen Funktionsumfang wie die ChatGPT-Apps für Windows und macOS. Wie Golem berichtet, ist Computer Use unter Linux noch nicht verfügbar. Die Funktion ermöglicht ChatGPT auf Windows und macOS, direkt mit anderen Desktop-Anwendungen zu interagieren und diese zu bedienen. Entsprechend fehlen unter Linux auch Funktionen, die darauf aufbauen. So lassen sich Inhalte geöffneter Desktop-Fenster nicht direkt an ChatGPT übergeben und Bildschirminhalte nicht aufzeichnen.
Ganz ohne Desktop-Integration startet die Linux-App aber nicht. Ein integrierter App Browser, die Unterstützung von Chrome-Erweiterungen und die Sprachsteuerung sind schon verfügbar.
Der Artikel stammt von Larissa Ceccio aus der OnlineMarketing.de-Redaktion und wird im Rahmen einer Content-Kooperation auf t3n veröffentlicht.

articles.title: Total eclipse of the Internet: Traffic impacts in Iceland, Spain, and Portugal
articles.text:
Total eclipse of the Internet: Traffic impacts in Iceland, Spain, and Portugal
At a time where looking down at our devices is a ritual in daily life, a natural phenomenon that demands our attention communally upward is a welcome event. On Wednesday, August 12, a total solar eclipse swept from the North Atlantic across Europe, moving over Iceland and northern Spain and Portugal, with a deep partial eclipse over the rest of western Europe, all near local sunset. This was the first total solar eclipse to cross mainland Europe in twenty years, and it drew millions outdoors to witness the moon pass between Earth and the sun.
As we saw during the 2026 World Cup and the last total eclipse in 2024, online behavior is noticeably affected when an event at this scale takes place. In this blog post, we’ll use data from Cloudflare Radar to examine how Internet traffic shifted alongside the moon and the sun.
Internet traffic dips align precisely with maximum obscuration
In the figure above, we measured HTTP request volume in five-minute buckets across the affected countries on eclipse day, and compared it to a normal-day baseline. Each row is a country (except for Alaska) and each column is a five-minute slice of August 12, the day of the eclipse. The countries appear above in the order in which they saw the eclipse.
The black diamonds mark the moment of maximum eclipse and the color shows the percent change in HTTP traffic versus the baseline (red = below normal, blue = above). We can see very clearly that the black diamonds overlay the darkest red, almost perfectly, signaling that as the eclipse deepened, Internet traffic decreased. The decrease was most significant along the path of totality and in countries that saw the deepest partial eclipse (Iceland, Ireland, the UK, France, Spain and Portugal) and all but absent where the sun was barely obscured (Sweden, Denmark, Poland, Switzerland).
Where the eclipse was deep, the red colour and black diamonds mirror each other: traffic falls into a trough that sits directly beneath the peak of obscuration and rebounds as the sun reappears, typically within minutes of maximum coverage as people return to their screens.
The scatter plot above suggests that these decreases are not due to random chance. Each point represents the peak solar obscuration of an individual country (x-axis), against the region's traffic dip (y-axis). The traffic dip is measured as the average percentage change versus baseline in the 15-minute window surrounding maximum eclipse. The downward trend of the dotted line following the dots demonstrates that regions along the path of totality saw traffic fall by roughly 15% to 30%, whereas areas experiencing only a shallow partial eclipse dipped far less or not at all. While local variables like population density, time of day, and cloud cover account for scatter at any given coverage level, the overall direction remains consistent. Paired with the precise timing of the drops, the trend of the data demonstrates that the eclipse itself was the primary driver of the decline.
Iceland, Spain and Portugal saw the biggest decreases in traffic
The figure above shows trend lines for each individual country. The gray triangles represent the progression of the eclipse obscuration, while the red line tracks the amount of traffic changed from its usual baseline. In almost all of the countries and regions impacted in the course of the eclipse, traffic made noteworthy changes ranging from 9.3 to -46.7%.
The right-hand numbers on the “y2”-axis are the obscuration, calculated using precise sun and moon positions. For each location we found the apparent angular sizes of the sun and moon and how far apart they are in the sky, then calculated the fraction of the sun's disk covered by the moon every 5 minutes via the geometric overlap of two circles. That gave each place both its peak obscuration (how deep the eclipse got, 0–100%) and its moment of maximum eclipse. We then summed all regions in each country for the traffic total, and took the average obscuration across a country's regions to place its national max-eclipse time.
To differentiate the eclipse from a typical Wednesday evening, we compared eclipse day against the same weekday: the median of the three previous Wednesdays, matched slot-by-slot on time-of-day. Using the median keeps one odd week from skewing the comparison. Every number is then reported as percent change vs. baseline. When looking at the percentage on the left hand y-axis, 0% means "totally normal" and negative means "less active than usual."
We can see the changes in traffic beginning in Alaska around 15:35 UTC, where the eclipse began its pathway. Iceland, Spain, and Portugal experienced the most dramatic drops in traffic, whereas Poland and Denmark quickly returned to pre-eclipse levels. Norway and Sweden actually saw slight traffic increases above baseline, while Denmark recorded the least overall change.
Ultimately, these findings reveal a clear correlation between the path of the eclipse and human behavior online. While the severity and duration of traffic drops varied by region, Radar’s HTTP traffic data demonstrates how a shared physical event can temporarily reshape digital activity across an entire continent.
Track the impact of world events on Cloudflare Radar
Major events in the physical world remind us that digital traffic is, at its core, a direct reflection of human attention. When the moon obscured the sun across Europe, the Internet slowed down not because of network failures, but because people paused their online activity to watch. As network patterns quickly normalized post-eclipse, the data left behind offers a fascinating snapshot of how a cosmic event can momentarily realign our online world.
To explore more interactive traffic insights and track how major worldwide events shape internet activity every day, visit Cloudflare Radar or follow us on social media at @CloudflareRadar (X), https://noc.social/@cloudflareradar (Mastodon), and @radar.cloudflare.com (Bluesky).

articles.title: Nightmare Eclipse Drops Windows Zero-Day Exploit ‘ShieldBreak’
articles.text:
Security researcher Nightmare Eclipse has dropped a fresh zero-day exploit leading to privilege escalation on Windows.
Also known as Chaotic Eclipse, the disgruntled researcher released multiple zero-day exploits targeting Microsoft products over the past several months, usually right after the Patch Tuesday security updates.
Right on cue, the new proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit, dubbed ShieldBreak, was published on August 2026 Patch Tuesday. It targets a vulnerability in Microsoft Defender, allowing any user to gain System privileges.
According to Nightmare Eclipse, the exploit is a RoguePlanet patch bypass, works on the latest Windows 11 versions and on Windows Server 2025, and likely impacts Windows 10 machines as well.
Tracked as CVE-2026-50656, RoguePlanet is a race condition flaw in Defender that Nightmare Eclipse dropped as a zero-day on June 9. Microsoft acknowledged the exploit on June 16 and released fixes for it on July 9.
Per the analysis of Tharros Labs’s Will Dormann, ShieldBreak involves setting up a temporary directory registered as a Cloud Sync provider, planting an EICAR file, controlling Defender’s scan path to System32, using Windows’ CLFS to swap the identity file and hydration data to a ‘phoneinfo.dll’ file in System32, then running the QueueReporting scheduled task.
“In the wer.dll code, there is explicit code to load phoneinfo.dll [which does not exist by default in Windows]. Because at this point, phoneinfo.dll exists and is our own code, this runs, spawning conhost.exe with SYSTEM privileges,” Dormann says.
Both Dormann and cybersecurity expert Kevin Beaumont, who published detection queries for the fresh PoC, disagree with Nightmare Eclipse’s assertion that ShieldBreak is a RoguePlanet bypass, as they work differently.
“RoguePlanet was a filesystem race condition vuln that uses virtual disks and NT native file manipulation to trick the quarantine process into overwriting system files. ShieldBreak user-mode callback hook to change file contents during a Defender cloud-hydration scan via cfapi (Cloud Filter API),” Beaumont said.
Dormann also points out that “ShieldBreak seems to require Defender to be active to work,” while RoguePlanet did not.
Related: SharePoint Vulnerability Exploited Shortly After PoC Release
Related: Chipmaker Patch Tuesday: Intel, AMD Fix Over 80 Vulnerabilities Combined
Related: Fresh Windows Zero-Day Exploited in North Korean Cyberattacks
Related: Ivanti EPM Update Patches Remotely Exploitable Flaws

articles.title: Quebra de plataforma deixa geleira da Antártida mais vulnerável
articles.text:
O colapso de plataformas de gelo na Antártida pode alterar o ritmo de avanço das geleiras e, consequentemente, as projeções de elevação do nível do mar. Pesquisadores do Caltech acompanharam esse processo durante nove anos com dados de satélites.
Publicado na revista Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, o estudo analisou a geleira Pine Island, na Antártida Ocidental. Os resultados mostram como o desprendimento de grandes blocos de gelo enfraquece estruturas que ajudam a conter seu fluxo.
A barreira que perdeu força
A Pine Island é a geleira de fluxo mais rápido da Antártida e a maior contribuidora da região para o aumento do nível do mar. Parte desse avanço é contida pela plataforma de gelo que se estende sobre o oceano.
Essa estrutura funciona como uma espécie de rolha. Ao exercer pressão sobre o gelo, ela reduz sua velocidade antes que a massa alcance o mar.
Em 2017, um grande bloco da plataforma se desprendeu e formou um iceberg. Depois do evento, a velocidade da Pine Island aumentou 20%. Desde 1973, o fluxo da geleira cresceu mais de 100%.
O gelo acumula danos
Para entender o processo, a equipe analisou imagens dos satélites de radar Sentinel-1, da Agência Espacial Europeia, registradas entre 2015 e 2024. O material permitiu acompanhar tanto o deslocamento da geleira quanto o estado de suas margens de cisalhamento, nas laterais.
Essas regiões funcionam como pontos de resistência. Quando perdem força, o gelo encontra menos oposição para avançar.
A sequência observada pelos pesquisadores foi:
- danos já estavam presentes antes de 2017;
- o desprendimento daquele ano intensificou as falhas;
- a geleira ganhou velocidade;
- o fluxo mais rápido aumentou a pressão nas margens;
- em 2020, a geleira estava completamente desacoplada das margens danificadas.
“Após esse evento de desprendimento, os danos simplesmente se intensificam”, afirmou Sarah Wells-Moran, autora principal do estudo. Segundo ela, o aumento da velocidade coloca mais força sobre as margens, gerando novos danos e acelerando ainda mais o gelo.
Reflexos nas previsões
A Pine Island avança cerca de 4,8 quilômetros por ano. Parece pouco, mas ela já é a maior contribuidora da Antártida para a elevação do nível do mar.
Leia mais:
- IA calcula quanto o mar subiria se todas as geleiras derretessem
- Como a NASA monitora o clima na Terra
- O gelo da Antártida está devolvendo ao mar um antigo poluente: o mercúrio
O comportamento observado oferece uma oportunidade para testar modelos que tentam prever o futuro da geleira. Ainda não se sabe, porém, exatamente como será o recuo nem qual será sua velocidade.
O futuro com níveis administráveis de elevação do nível do mar e os cenários extremos depende do comportamento da camada de gelo da Antártida Ocidental.
Brent Minchew, professor de geofísica do Caltech, em nota.
A expectativa é que modelos mais precisos ajudem a antecipar mudanças na região e forneçam uma base mais confiável para o planejamento de comunidades e estruturas próximas ao litoral.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Mozilla’s CTO thinks AI should be built like the internet
articles.text:
For decades, Mozilla has been one of the strongest advocates for an open internet. Today, as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly central to how businesses and governments operate, the organization is making a similar case for open AI.
In a report published last month, Mozilla, a free software community and nonprofit project, said the performance gap between top open-source models and proprietary systems like Claude and ChatGPT has narrowed to just 3%. The report highlighted the growing popularity of open models, noting that in February 2026, Alibaba’s open-source model Qwen was downloaded more times than the next eight models combined.
The debate over open AI has gained fresh momentum after Meta released a new open-weight model on August 10, and promised more would come soon.
Raffi Krikorian, Mozilla’s chief technology officer, believes organizations need alternatives to proprietary AI systems to gain greater control over their data and infrastructure.
Throughout his career — from leading engineering teams at X (then Twitter) to working on autonomous vehicles at Uber and now shaping Mozilla’s vision — Krikorian has worked on breakthrough technologies and what they mean for consumers. In a conversation with Rest of World, he discussed why policymakers need to view AI as infrastructure rather than as a product, why businesses are increasingly experimenting with open and open-weight models, and what role he believes the technology will play in the next generation of products and services.
The conversation has been edited for length and clarity. A recording of the live Rest of World event is available here.
You’ve said that open-source AI is no longer a “hobbyist ecosystem” and that it has a multi-hundred-billion-dollar commercial layer. What have you based this finding on?
When you talk about open source in certain circles, usually governmental policy circles, they would say things like, “Oh, it’s just some kid in the basement, right?” This ecosystem is not that. These businesses are building huge economies, infrastructure, products, and technology.
It’s like Linux, which started with just a kernel, not being taken very seriously. But Google was able to take Linux and make Android, and now, for all practical purposes, every computer on the planet runs on Linux. Every single new vending machine probably is running on Linux.
We are seeing the same thing in the open-source, open-weight AI world. It is because of the marketing blitz of the big frontier labs that we all view AI just as something that Anthropic, OpenAI, and a few other companies are doing. There’s actually a burgeoning ecosystem on the open-source, open-weight side that a lot of people actually do know about.
It’s potentially one of the best well-kept secrets right now when it comes to technology.
Why are more people not familiar with open-source tools?
There’s a difference between what consumers are doing and what businesses are starting to do.
It is true that an individual — like a secretary or another white-collar worker — is probably using ChatGPT and Claude. But the workflows that an IT or HR team is starting to put together are migrating toward open models because of price-performance reasons or potentially because of regulated industries, which want to have full control of their data and how their data flows. They want to self-host and have things stay within their firewall. They’re looking for an ability to deploy things under their control.
I don’t have a good answer as to why people aren’t shouting from their rooftops that they’re saving all this money.
Are people not talking about open-source models openly because many of them are Chinese and there are regulatory or trust issues with these tools?
We don’t have concrete proof that it’s true, but I think you can probably infer that to be true.
Open-source AI models are complicated to understand, and I think that is also part of the issue. When you look at these models, it’s like downloading a model you want to run, like a file, onto your computer. So, I can understand how people might — if they don’t truly understand how this technology works — be worried about just downloading malware that could be giving their data over in some places.
That’s not how the systems actually work. But the simplest explanation is the one that usually ends up winning.
And I also do believe that something about just China in general is confounding the equation a little bit. The confounding thing should be why aren’t more countries and organizations trying to fill that demand? If a large amount of traffic is going to a model that people want to be open, then you can imagine a world where American companies or Indian companies or European companies should also be trying to fill that demand.
In the context of the concerns with Chinese software, do you think governments — especially Washington — understand that open source is getting so popular?
I do think that the government understands what is happening. But they’re caught between “do we want to let our current existing standards bearers win” or “do we want to potentially take the risk and try to be a transformative thing to the ecosystem.”
I think it’s a simple thing to comprehend that we have two companies that are doing incredibly well, that are racing toward public listings either end of this year or the beginning of next year, and we want them to win. And the government is being lobbied very heavily in that regard.
So the simple thing to do would be to back the people they perceive to be the winners already.
But I would say that Americans have generally filed intelligence as a product. Products are by definition things that you can rent or turn off, but it should be filed as infrastructure, which is what the rest of the world seems to want to buy. That categorization error is actually the problem. We should be trying to fill that demand in some way, and I’m frustrated that my government can’t see that distinction right now, and they’re doing the simple thing.
Is open source really open for everyone?
I will admit that we are glossing over the open-source, open-weights conversation. There is the strictest definition of open source, which would come down to understanding all the data that went into training it on, all the evaluation systems, and what pre-training and post-training look like. I think that’s incredibly important, and we need to invest more in making that happen. That is what will lead to trust and transparency, and we can ethically feel really good about them.
Right now, a lot of what we’ve been talking about is open-weight systems. So we don’t have a good sense of all the data — pre-training and post-training. But what we do have is the ability to download, run, execute, and then modify and fine-tune. That fine-tune is where the rest of the world comes into play. The pathway to have really local models and local AI that reflect the value of the users is to take these big open-weight models and fine-tune them to our use cases in terms of the language we speak or the values of a community. The technology there still needs work. So, if you’re a computer scientist, you could probably do it, but if you’re a community leader, you probably can’t.
I’m not faulting what the big companies are doing, but they are going to optimize for the places where they can make the most money. So they’re going to optimize for the Western world and maybe parts of Asia, but they’re not going to optimize for the rest of the world. The rest of the world only becomes part of this AI transformative conversation through the open-source and open-weight ecosystem.
Mozilla has championed the open web for decades. Yet, Google has 90% of search, Meta has captured social media, and Amazon runs most of the cloud. Why should anyone believe that open-source AI would end differently?
The existence of things like Firefox has moved the entire industry. Someone like Google can’t build a closed version of the web because the vocal community of Firefox users will rise up and say you just can’t do that. Those types of numbers are enough to force and keep the internet in an open-protocol state and one that doesn’t benefit any particular company at that base infrastructure level.
I want the exact same dynamic to occur on the AI internet. You could make an argument that we get a small amount of traffic on the AI internet through the open models, but that would be enough to force a conversation around model choice, agentic harness choice, user agency, and making sure that memory stays on my side, not the user side. You can make the argument that it only takes a small amount of traffic to pull that off, but I’m also saying a large amount of traffic is already moving to the open model.
What do you think the biggest AI company of 2031 would be doing? Building models, memory, developer tools, agents, infrastructure, or something entirely different?
I think there will be a diffusion. We are going to find that the biggest provider is the one that provides an open version of intelligence that every single company can use and customize — similar to how we have a Google Drive subscription or a Microsoft Office 365 solution right now. It will be a services provider that can walk into a company and help them actually get over that hump and use AI.

articles.title: Affiché à -60 %, ce chargeur sans fil Qi2 2-en-1 peut recharger un iPhone et une Apple Watch en même temps — Frandroid
articles.text:
Satechi propose probablement l’un des chargeurs sans fil Qi2 les plus originaux du marché. Son bien nommé modèle OnTheGo 2-en-1 se présente sous la forme d’un petit boîtier pliable qui renferme deux surfaces magnétiques permettant de recharger simultanément un smartphone compatible Qi2 et une Apple Watch. Et l’objet rentre facilement dans une poche une fois replié. S’il vous intéresse, sachez qu’il profite d’une réduction de 60 %.
Ce qui rend le chargeur 2-en-1 Satechi intéressant
- Un double chargeur compact et léger
- Compatible avec la norme Qi2
- Une puissance de charge max de 15 W
Initialement affiché à 89,99 euros, le chargeur à induction Satechi OnTheGo 2-en-1 est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 35,99 euros sur Amazon.
Un chargeur sans fil à induction qui se fait oublier dans une poche
Le Satechi OnTheGo 2-en-1 se présente sous la forme d’un petit galet tout rond qui, une fois ouvert, dévoile un premier module magnétique destiné à accueillir un iPhone MagSafe ou un autre smartphone compatible Qi2, ainsi qu’un second cercle dédié à l’Apple Watch. Il peut ainsi recharger deux appareils simultanément. Déplié, le chargeur ne mesure que 15,46 cm de long, contre 7,43 cm une fois replié. De plus, il ne pèse que 103,1 g et son épaisseur une fois plié ne dépasse pas 2,26 cm : autant dire qu’il rentre facilement dans une poche et s’emporte facilement partout.
Grâce à son format pliable, le chargeur peut être utilisé de différentes façons. Déplié, il peut recharger le smartphone et la montre connectée côte à côte. Replié, il devient bien plus compact, puisque la montre se retrouve comme fixée à l’arrière du smartphone pendant la recharge. Pas de panique, vos appareils resteront bien positionnés pendant la recharge grâce aux aimants qu’intègre le chargeur, qui garantissent un meilleur alignement et une recharge plus efficace.
Une charge assez rapide pour les iPhone
Le pad principal peut donc accueillir des appareils compatibles Qi, Qi2 et MagSafe. Attention, si vous possédez un appareil Android, vous devrez peut-être vous équiper d’une coque compatible Qi2 pour bénéficier de l’alignement magnétique. Sur ce cercle destiné aux smartphones, le chargeur peut délivrer une puissance de 15 W maximum. Le module Apple Watch, qui utilise le système de charge magnétique propre à la tocante de la marque à la pomme, est quant à lui limité à 5 W.
Si vous rechargez en même temps un iPhone 16 et une Apple Watch Series 10, les deux appareils atteignent 50 % de batterie en 45 minutes pour l’iPhone et 40 minutes pour la montre, selon la marque. Retenez bien que le module Apple Watch ne prend pas en charge les montres connectées d’autres fabricants. En revanche, vous pouvez y poser un boîtier d’AirPods pour le recharger, si vous le souhaitez.
Si vous souhaitez découvrir d’autres modèles que nous recommandons, nous vous invitons dès maintenant à consulter notre guide des meilleurs chargeurs sans fil à induction du moment.

articles.title: Class Is in Session: GeForce NOW Levels Up Linux, Chromebooks and More
articles.text:
GeForce NOW is giving cloud gaming an extra-credit upgrade just in time for back-to-school season.
The native Linux app for GeForce NOW is officially out of beta. GeForce NOW is also delivering new cloud optimizations that make Frame Generation feel even more responsive while streaming. On top of that, Performance members will see higher frame rates in demanding games thanks to a CPU performance adjustment.
Plus, learn how GeForce NOW can add high-performance GeForce RTX gaming to the Chromebooks students already rely on for school – and how eligible new owners can take advantage of Chromebook Fast Pass.
It all adds up to more ways to move from assignments to adventures across nearly any device.
The only homework left is to decide what to play. This week, nine new games join the GeForce NOW library.
The Cloud Gets Extra Credit
GeForce NOW keeps getting better.
The native Linux app for GeForce NOW has officially graduated from beta. Built on months of community feedback, the release focuses on performance, stability and polish while continuing to support Ubuntu 24.04 and later. A new Flatpack repository makes getting started and receiving future updates even easier. Visit the download page for more information and instructions.
The cloud handles the rendering, so Linux gamers can tap into the latest GeForce RTX performance while staying on their preferred setup — without local hardware upgrades, compatibility headaches or complicated workarounds.
GeForce NOW has also optimized DLSS Frame Generation in the cloud, reducing latency and making games feel more responsive. The improvements are especially noticeable when streaming at 60 or 120 frames per second in 1440p and 4K, helping every mouse movement and camera pan feel more immediate.
Performance members will also enjoy additional server software optimizations to improve frame rates in select CPU-intensive games, helping demanding titles run more smoothly while delivering an even better gameplay experience. The cloud-side upgrade happens automatically, with nothing for members to install or configure, and at no additional cost.
From Class Mode to Game Mode
Chromebooks already in backpacks can double as a PC gaming powerhouse, with GeForce NOW giving everyday school setups extra credit.
Chromebooks handling lectures, group projects and browser tabs can transform into high-performance GeForce RTX gaming PCs in just a few clicks.
When class is out, open a supported browser or app and stream more than 2,000 supported PC games from existing libraries, with the cloud handling the heavy lifting. The same flexibility extends to Macs, Surface devices, everyday laptops, Steam Deck and mobile devices.
Plus, eligible new Chromebook and Chromebook+ owners can claim a year of GeForce NOW at no cost with Chromebook Fast Pass, with priority access and no ads.
Study. Stream PC games. Same device.
